subsystems.name: Polymer matrix
subsystems.role: the bulk material that carries load and holds the healing agents.
parts: bio-based resin (plant-oil, starch, PLA or PHA derived)

subsystems.name: Healing-agent payload
subsystems.role: the dormant biological or chemical contents that do the repair.
parts: nutrient feedstock such as calcium lactate or yeast extract
healing monomer plus catalyst, in purely chemical systems

subsystems.name: Encapsulation and carriers
subsystems.role: protect the payload during mixing, curing and years of service, then release it on demand.
parts: porous lightweight aggregate or expanded clay carrier

subsystems.name: Trigger and release
subsystems.role: convert a mechanical crack into a chemical release.
parts: pH and ionic-strength change at the crack face

subsystems.name: Healing chemistry
subsystems.role: turns the released payload into solid material that bridges the crack.

subsystems.name: Verification instrumentation
subsystems.role: shows that healing actually happened and how completely.

buildSteps.title: Select and culture the strain
buildSteps.detail: Choose a bacterium that forms tough spores, tolerates the alkaline chemistry of cement or the pH of the resin, and precipitates carbonate. Grow it in liquid culture, then starve it so it sporulates.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Mix the nutrient and calcium sources in the right ratio — typically a calcium salt of an organic acid, which the bacteria metabolise into carbonate while supplying the calcium to bind it.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the payload
buildSteps.detail: Freeze-dry the spores and lock them into a carrier — coated hydrogel beads, porous aggregate soaked in spore suspension, or brittle microcapsules made by emulsion polymerisation with a shell thin enough to crack but tough enough to survive mixing.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the matrix
buildSteps.detail: Blend the bio-based resin or cementitious binder with a few percent by weight of loaded capsules, plus catalyst and filler. The loading must be high enough to heal cracks yet low enough not to weaken the material.

buildSteps.title: Shape and cure
buildSteps.detail: Cast, mould, extrude or spray the mixture. Curing temperatures and shear must stay below the point where capsules rupture or spores die.

buildSteps.title: Trigger healing
buildSteps.detail: When a crack opens, it tears open the capsules in its path. Water reaches the spores, which germinate, and the healing chemistry starts.

buildSteps.title: Precipitate the repair mineral
buildSteps.detail: The bacteria consume the nutrient, raise the local carbonate concentration, and calcium carbonate crystallises in the crack, gradually sealing it against water and air.

buildSteps.title: Verify and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Measure strength recovery, water tightness and crack closure, and confirm the spores stayed viable over months of storage and service.

prerequisites.why: the payload must survive drying, mixing and an aggressive matrix chemistry, then wake up decades later.
shells must rupture on cracking but never during processing or normal loading.
plant-oil, starch, PLA and PHA resins give a renewable matrix, though some are moisture-sensitive.
infrastructure lifetimes run to decades, and few field trials have run long enough to prove survival.
a healing event deep inside a structure cannot be seen, so it must be inferred from sensors.

pathway.milestone: microcapsule-based autonomic healing demonstrated in polymer composites; bacterial self-healing studied in cementitious materials
pathway.unlocks: proof that a material can repair its own cracks without human intervention.

pathway.milestone: self-healing admixtures trialled in concrete walls, tunnel linings, marine structures and coatings
pathway.unlocks: real service data on crack widths healed, strength recovery and durability.

pathway.milestone: commercial self-healing additives and coatings for high-wear and hard-to-reach infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: repair in places nobody can access — foundations, tunnels, offshore structures.

pathway.milestone: standardised test methods and design codes that credit self-healing in service life
pathway.unlocks: wider adoption, longer maintenance intervals and thinner, lighter structures.
